chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from one of our companions, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed Samurat ibn Jundab had a date palm, and its pathway to it was in the middle of the house of a man from the Ansar. So he used to come and enter to his palm without permission from the Ansari. So the Ansari said to him, 'O Samurat! You do not cease to surprise us upon a state which we do not like to be surprised upon. So whenever you enter, seek permission.' So he said, 'I will not seek permission regarding a pathway, and it is my pathway to my palm.'

So the Ansari complained to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent for him, so he came to him. So he (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'So-and-so has complained about you and alleged that you pass by him and his family without his permission. So seek permission from him whenever you intend to enter.' So he said, 'O Messenger of Allah! Do I seek permission regarding my pathway to my palm?'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Leave it alone, and for you will be its place, a palm in such and such a place.' So he said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'For you will be two.' He said, 'I do not want it.'

So he (peace be upon him and his family) did not cease to increase for him until it reached ten palms. So he said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'For you will be ten in such and such a place.' But he refused. So he (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Leave it alone, and for you will be its place, a palm in Paradise.' He said, 'I do not want it.'
So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Indeed you are a harmful man, and there should neither be a harm nor a harm caused upon a Believer.'

Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered with it, so it was uprooted, then it was thrown at him, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Go, and plant it wherever you desire.'

key_terms.لَا ضَرَرَ وَ لَا ضِرَارَ: No harm and no causing harm (a fundamental legal maxim)
key_terms.مُضَارٌّ: One who causes harm or is stubbornly harmful

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a pathway crossing another's property if the owner refuses compensation?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *Idhar* (stubbornness) through Samurat ibn Jundab’s refusal of multiple compensations for his right of way, highlighting that legal rights can be forfeited by excessive insistence. The Prophet’s final verdict, 'There is no harm nor causing harm' (*La darara wa la dirar*), serves as a foundational juristic maxim in Shia fiqh for resolving property disputes. The narrative underscores that the right of way is not absolute if it imposes undue burden (*darar*) on the property owner.
